summary:
The IBM 1410 (1411 Processing Unit) is a variable-word-length, character-addressed, BCD decimal machine with 5-character decimal addresses, add-to-storage arithmetic, and word marks that delimit fields. Instruction lengths are 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, or 12 characters, built from an op-code character O, a 5-char A-address, a 5-char B-address, a 3-char X-control field (I/O), and a 1-char d-modifier (A22-0526-2 p.11). Omitted addresses are *chained*: the A- and B-address registers (AAR/BAR) retain whatever the previous instruction left in them, so every op's documented 'address registers after operation' is load-bearing for an emulator. A two-address instruction that takes no d-character (an 11-position instruction) blanks the op-modifier register, so a following chained instruction inherits a blank d (p.12). Every instruction must carry a word mark over its op code.

Data movement on the 1410 is unified into ONE op code, D, whose d-character is a 6-bit control word: the 4/2/1 bits select which portion of each character moves (1 = numeric, 2 = zone, 4 = word mark; no 1/2/4 bits = scan, no data transferred), and the B/A/8 bits select direction and terminator (8 bit = left-to-right, no 8 bit = right-to-left; then no B/A = 'one position' (R-L) or 'first WM in either field' (L-R); A only = A-field WM (R-L) / A-field record mark (L-R); B only = B-field WM (R-L) / A-field group-mark-word-mark (L-R); B and A = first WM in either field (R-L) / A-field RM or GM-WM (L-R)). All 64 d-characters are valid, giving the 64 Autocoder mnemonics MLxx / MRxx / SCNxx (Figures 19-22, pp.25-27). The terminating character itself is moved/replaced like any other. Move Characters and Suppress Zeros (Z) and Move Characters and Edit (E) are separate ops; there is no 'Load' op (the 1401 Load Characters is expressed as MLCWA/MLCWB, i.e. D with the word-mark bit set), no Move-and-Insert-Zeros, and no Translate/Convert op in the base 1410 instruction set.

Arithmetic is add-to-storage in the B field with sign in the zone bits of the units position: minus is always a B bit; plus is BA, A, or no zone; a machine-developed plus sign is always BA (Figure 11, p.16). Add/Subtract choose true-add or complement-add from the two signs (Figure 12, p.16) and the result takes the sign of the greater value, with a recomplement pass when the complement-add underflows (the R term in the timing formulas, Figure 7, p.12). Digits outside 0-9 are coerced: blank becomes 0 (8+2 bits) and characters with numeric bits summing above 9 have the 8 bit dropped (p.16). Multiply requires the multiplier image pre-placed in the HIGH-order positions of the B (product) field and B length = digits(multiplicand) + digits(multiplier) + 1; sign is like-signs-plus, unlike-signs-minus, and the multiplier image is destroyed. Divide addresses the units position of the divisor (A) and the LEFTMOST position of the dividend (B); B length = digits(divisor) + digits(dividend) + 1, the quotient field must be pre-zeroed and the dividend must be signed - the recommended setup is a Zero and Add of the dividend into the B field, which supplies both the zeros and the BA/B sign. Quotient lands leftmost, remainder rightmost with the sign of the original dividend; division by zero always sets divide overflow.

Indicators: arithmetic overflow (tested/reset by J(I)Z) when a sum exceeds the B-field word mark; zero balance (J(I)V) set by add, subtract, multiply, zero-and-add, zero-and-subtract and reset by the next such op that is not a zero balance (divide never affects it); divide overflow (J(I)W); and the compare high/equal/low/unequal latches (J(I)U / J(I)S / J(I)T / J(I)/), set by Compare, Table Lookup and Branch if Character Equal, and reset only by the next one of those three. Overflow indicators are turned off by the branch that tests them or by computer reset; computer reset also clears zero-balance and turns ON low-compare and unequal-compare. Timing is 4.5 us per storage cycle, expressed as formulas in the per-op rows; the 1410 Accelerator feature substitutes a different (faster) timing table.

facts.claim: IBM 1410 instruction formats are exactly: O (1), Od (2), O xxx d (5), O aaaaa (6), O aaaaa d (7), O xxx bbbbb d (10), O aaaaa bbbbb (11), O aaaaa bbbbb d (12) characters. a=5-char A address, b=5-char B address, xxx=X-control field, d=op modifier.
facts.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation, A22-0526-2, p.11 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-2_1410_PrincOps.pdf (OCR: https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_13458542/A22-0526-2_1410_PrincOps_djvu.txt)

facts.claim: Omitting addresses chains the instruction: the op code alone reuses the A- and B-address registers left by the previous operation. If a two-address instruction takes no d-character (11-position form), the op-modifier register is blanked, so any chained instruction that follows gets a blank d-character.

Address-register symbols used in the per-op 'after operation' rows: A/B = the instruction's A/B address; NSI = next sequential instruction; BI = branch-to address; NSIB = address of instruction following a taken branch; LA/LB = A-/B-field length; LW = length of the shorter field; Ap/Bp = previous contents of AAR/BAR.

Timing symbols: A = A-field length, B = B-field length, C = 1 if branch taken, D = chars in B field from start of zero suppression to the dollar-sign insert point (0 if none), E = 2 on a 1-char multiply or divide, 1 on a 1-char add/subtract/zero-and-add/zero-and-subtract/table-lookup or a 6-char multiply/divide, else 0; L = instruction length; M = multiplier length; N = number of fields actually compared on a table search; Q = quotient length; R = 1 if a recomplement is taken on add/subtract; Z = chars in B field from start of zero suppression to the left end of the B field. All times in microseconds; basic storage cycle 4.5 us.

Sign convention: the sign of a field is the zone bits of its UNITS position. Minus is always a B bit. Plus may be B+A bits, no zone bits, or (less commonly) an A bit alone. When the machine develops or changes a sign, plus is always written as B and A bits.

Add/Subtract cycle selection and result sign: ADD with like signs = true-add, result keeps that sign; ADD with unlike signs = complement-add, result takes the sign of the greater value. SUBTRACT inverts the A-field sign first, then the same rule applies (A+ B- = true-add, A+ B+ = complement-add, A- B+ = complement-add, A- B- = true-add).

Digit coding in arithmetic: characters whose numeric bits total 0-9 (all numerals, all letters, and / ? ! and the group mark) participate normally; all other characters have numeric bits changed from blank to zero (8 and 2 bits) or reduced into range by dropping the 8 bit. Example: group mark (CBA8421) added to zero becomes G (BA421) if zones retained, or 7 (421) if zones stripped; # (821) becomes 3.
Arithmetic overflow: if the result exceeds the B-field limit set by the B-field word mark, the carry is lost and the arithmetic overflow indicator turns on. Tested and turned off by J (I) Z (BAV).

Zero balance: set by any add, subtract, multiply, zero-and-add, or zero-and-subtract whose result is a zero balance; tested by J (I) V (BZ); turned off by the next arithmetic instruction (any except divide) that does not produce a zero balance. Divide does not affect it.

Overflow indicators are turned off by the specific branch instruction that tests them, or by a computer reset. Computer reset also turns off the zero-result indicator and turns ON the low-compare and unequal-compare indicators.
Indexing does not set the arithmetic overflow latch even if the index addition overflows.

Add two fields: A aaaaa bbbbb (11) or chained 1-char. Sum stored in B. B-field zone bits unchanged except the sign position; A-field zone bits ignored except the sign position. Ends on the B-field word mark (required). A-field word mark needed only if A is shorter than B, in which case zeros are supplied to the extra high-order B positions up to and including the B word mark. A-field positions beyond the B word mark are not processed. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=A-LW, BAR=B-LB. T = 4.5(L+1+E+A+1.5B+1.5RB); E=1 when L=1, E=0 when L=11.

Add one field: A aaaaa (6). The A field is image-added to itself (doubled) and stored back in A. Zone bits and the sign bit configuration are unchanged. Ends on the A-field word mark. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=A-LA, BAR=A-LA. T = 4.5(L+1+A+1.5A), L = 1 or 6.

Subtract one field: S aaaaa (6) subtracts the A field from itself, leaving a zeroed result in A with zone bits and sign configuration unchanged (example: A-field ABQ becomes ??!). Ends on the A-field word mark. After: AAR=BAR=A-LA.

Zero and Add two fields (? aaaaa bbbbb): numeric data of A stored in B with A's sign; zone bits stripped from all B positions except the sign; a plus sign not already B+A is rewritten as B+A. Ends on the B-field word mark; short A field zero-fills high-order B up to and including its word mark. After: AAR=A-LW, BAR=B-LB. T = 4.5(L+1+E+A+1.5B).

Zero and Subtract two fields (! aaaaa bbbbb) sign map: A no-zone (plus) -> B minus (B bit); A B-bit (minus) -> B plus (B and A bits); A B+A (plus) -> B minus (B bit); A A-bit (plus) -> B minus (B bit).

Multiply (@ aaaaa bbbbb): A field is the multiplicand addressed at its UNITS position; the B field is the product field addressed at its UNITS position, and the multiplier image must already sit in the HIGH-order positions of B. Required B length = digits(multiplicand) + digits(multiplier) + 1. Word marks must define the high-order position of the multiplicand and of the multiplier image in the product field. The first scan zeros the product positions to the right of the multiplier; the multiplier image is decremented and destroyed as the product develops. After: AAR=A-LA, BAR=B-LB. T ~ 4.5[L+1+E+2.5M+(2.5M+1.5)(2.5A+3)], L = 1, 6 or 11.

Multiply sign and zones: zones in the multiplicand are undisturbed; zones anywhere in the assigned product area are eliminated before product development; zones in the multiplier are eliminated during development. Signs of the units position of the multiplicand and of the multiplier are sampled first: like signs give a plus product, unlike signs a minus product, written into the units (sign) position of B at the end.

Multiply algorithm: multiplier digit 1-4 causes that many true-adds of the multiplicand (digit decremented each cycle, zero ends the group and shifts left one position); digit 5-9 causes tens-complement complement-adds in the low-order positions followed by a left shift and a true-add starting in the tens position (e.g. multiplier digit 8 costs three cycles, not eight).

Divide (% aaaaa bbbbb): A-address = UNITS position of the divisor; B-address = LEFTMOST position of the dividend (i.e. of the quotient-dividend field). Required B length = digits(divisor) + digits(dividend) + 1. The quotient field must contain zeros at start, and the dividend must be signed (B+A for plus, B for minus) - the sign stops the division. Moving the dividend in with a Zero and Add supplies both. A word mark must define the leftmost position of the divisor; the B-field word mark left by the Zero and Add is ignored but retained. After: AAR=A-LA, BAR=tens position of the quotient field. T ~ 4.5{L+1+E+6.5Q[A+1.5(A+2)]}, L = 1, 6 or 11.

Divide results: quotient in the leftmost positions of B (units position of quotient = address of units of dividend minus length of divisor minus one); remainder in the rightmost positions of B; quotient sign by algebraic rule (like signs plus, unlike minus); remainder sign = sign of the original dividend.

Divide overflow: tested by J (I) W (BDV). A quotient field one position too small does NOT raise overflow (it silently corrupts the adjacent field); two or more positions short usually does. Division by zero always raises divide overflow. Too-small a quotient field is a programming error and is not checked.

Store Address Register (G ccccc d): stores the 5-character contents of the register named by d into the C field, C-address = RIGHTMOST position of the destination. d = A (AAR), B (BAR), E (E register), F (F register). E and F hold tape addresses in overlap mode. The C-address uses the C-address register, so the A-address register is NOT disturbed. Word marks in the C field have no effect; zones in the C field are not disturbed. This instruction cannot be indexed. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=Ap, BAR=Bp. T = 69.75 us.

Store Address Register d = T stores the Program Addressable Clock (real-time clock): high-order digit 0 or 9, hours in continental time, minutes as hundredths of an hour (1:30 pm = 01350). This is the Program Addressable Clock special feature, not base 1410.
facts.source: IBM 1410 CE Handbook 223-2588-2 (1964-04) p.25 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf ; feature manual G22-6654

facts.claim: Set Word Mark op code is comma (','), Autocoder SW. Forms: , aaaaa bbbbb (sets WM at both A and B), , aaaaa (A only), and no-address chained (sets WMs at the locations currently in AAR and BAR). Data characters are not disturbed. After: two addresses -> AAR=A-1, BAR=B-1; one address -> AAR=BAR=A-1; no address -> AAR=Ap-1, BAR=Bp-1. T = 4.5(L+4), L = 1, 6 or 11.
facts.source: A22-0526-2 p.22 and Appendix p.104; op-code character confirmed by CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.16 and SimH i7000_defs.h CHR_COM=033

facts.claim: Clear Word Mark op code is the lozenge character (BCD BA84, card 12-8-4, rendered in the manuals as a small square/diamond), Autocoder CW. Same three forms and same register results as Set Word Mark; clears the word mark if present, data undisturbed. T = 4.5(L+4).
facts.source: A22-0526-2 p.22, Appendix p.102; SimH i7010_defs.h OP_CWM = CHR_LPARN = 074 octal = BA84

facts.claim: Clear Storage (/ bbbbb): clears data AND word marks right-to-left from the B address down to and including the nearest hundreds position. Example: / 12590 clears 12590..12500 and leaves BAR = 12499. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=B, BAR=bbb00-1. With no address the current BAR is used and the AAR is not loaded and is undisturbed. T = 4.5(L+1+B), L = 1 or 6.
Clear Storage and Branch (/ iiiii bbbbb): same clearing effect as Clear Storage, then unconditionally takes the next instruction from the I-address. After: IAR=NSIB, AAR=BI, BAR=NSIB. T = 4.5(L+2+B).

Halt op code is period ('.'), Autocoder H. 1-character form stops the system; pressing Start resumes with the next sequential instruction. T = 4.5. After: AAR=Ap, BAR=Bp. Halt and Branch is . iiiii (6 chars): stops, and Start resumes at the I-address (unconditional branch). T = 36. After: IAR=NSIB, AAR=BI, BAR=NSIB. If a halt is the last instruction in the program a word mark must be preset in the position immediately to the right of it.
facts.source: A22-0526-2 p.23; CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.16; SimH i7010_defs.h OP_H = CHR_DOT = 073 octal

facts.claim: No Operation op code is N. It can be written over the op code of any instruction to make that instruction ineffective; the instruction's remaining characters are skipped, so L is 1, 2, 3 ... no limit. Word marks not affected. After: AAR=Ap, BAR=Bp. T = 4.5(L+1).

All 1410 data movement uses one op code, D, with a 6-bit d-character. 4/2/1 bits select the portion moved: 1 = numeric portion, 2 = zone portion, 4 = word marks from A to B, none of 1/2/4 = scan (A and B address registers stepped, no data transferred). B/A/8 bits select direction and terminator. All 64 d-characters are valid.

Move terminator/direction encoding. With the 8 bit set the move is LEFT-TO-RIGHT and: no B and no A = stop at first word mark sensed in either field; A bit only = stop at A-field record mark; B bit only = stop at A-field group-mark-word-mark; B and A = stop at A-field record mark or group-mark-word-mark. With no 8 bit the move is RIGHT-TO-LEFT and: no B and no A = transfer or scan only one storage position; A bit only = stop at A-field word mark; B bit only = stop at B-field word mark; B and A = stop at first word mark sensed in either field.
facts.source: A22-0526-2 Figure 19, p.25; cross-checked against CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.23 and SimH i7010_cpu.c case OP_MOV (switch on op_mod & 070)

facts.claim: Move addressing and effect: for a left-to-right move the A- and B-addresses are the LEFTMOST positions of their fields; for a right-to-left move they are the RIGHTMOST positions. Only the selected portion of the A character replaces the corresponding portion of the B character; the rest of the B character is unchanged. The position holding the terminating character is moved/replaced like every other position.

Move address registers after operation. Left-to-right: stop-at-first-WM-either-field -> AAR = A+LW, BAR = B+LW; the three record-oriented terminators (A-field RM, A-field GM-WM, either) -> AAR = A+LA, BAR = B+LA. Right-to-left: one position -> AAR = A-1, BAR = B-1; stop at A-field WM -> A-LA / B-LA; stop at B-field WM -> A-LB / B-LB; stop at first WM either field -> A-LW / B-LW. IAR = NSI in all cases.

Move instruction lengths: L = 1, 6 or 12. A 6-character D instruction (D aaaaa) chains the B-address and reuses the last previous operation modifier. T = 4.5(L+1+A+1.5B). Same length rule and chaining note apply to Table Lookup (T).

Move mnemonic construction: move mnemonics are M + direction (L = right-to-left, R = left-to-right) + portion (N numeric, Z zone, C character = zone+numeric, W word mark, or the pairs NW/ZW/CW) + terminator (A = A-field WM, B = B-field WM, blank = first WM either field, S = one position, R = A-field record mark, G = A-field group-mark-word-mark, M = A-field RM or GM-WM). Scan mnemonics are SCN + direction (L/R) + terminator.

Move Characters and Suppress Zeros (Z aaaaa bbbbb, Autocoder MCS): moves A to B, A unchanged; high-order zeros and commas in the B field are replaced by blanks and the zone bits in the units (sign) position of B are removed. The A field must have a defining word mark, which sets the length moved; B-field word marks inside the moved area, including its leftmost position, are removed. Alphabetic and most special characters (e.g. @) count as non-significant, so zero suppression can restart to the right of them. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=A-LA, BAR=B+1. T = 4.5(L+1+4A), L = 1, 6 or 11.

Move Characters and Suppress Zeros scans the A field right-to-left (A- and B-addresses are the units positions), then makes a left-to-right suppression pass over the B field, leaving BAR one position to the right of the B address.
facts.source: Inferred from the documented AAR=A-LA / BAR=B+1 result (A22-0526-2 p.27) and confirmed by SimH i7010_cpu.c case OP_MSZ, which does DownReg(AAR)/DownReg(BAR) on the copy pass then UpReg(BAR) and scans forward suppressing zeros, blanks and commas, stopping suppression at a significant digit and treating '-' and '.' as pass-through

facts.claim: Compare (C aaaaa bbbbb): compares B to A, never A to B. All BA8421 bits are compared; C (check) bits and word marks are not. Neither field is changed. Sets high (B>A), equal (B=A), low (B<A) indicators; the unequal indicator accompanies high or low. Result must be tested before the next Compare, Table Lookup, or Branch if Character Equal, which resets all four. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=A-LW, BAR=B-LW. T = 4.5(L+1+A+B), L = 1, 6 or 11.

Compare terminates on either an A-field or a B-field word mark. If the A field is SHORTER than the B field the high indicator is turned on. If the B field is shorter than or equal in length to the A field, the indicators are set correctly for the portions actually compared.

Table Lookup (T aaaaa bbbbb d): searches right-to-left through the table for a table argument that is equal/high/low relative to the search argument, per d. A-address = rightmost position of the search argument; B-address = rightmost character of the entire table. Each table field is an implicit B field with the argument in its rightmost positions and the function in its leftmost positions. Search argument (A field) must have a word mark at its leftmost position; each table field must have a defining word mark at its leftmost position. The A-field word mark stops each argument comparison; if no hit, comparison restarts one position to the left of the table field's word mark. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=A-LW, BAR = address of the function immediately to the left of the table argument that stopped the operation. T = 4.5(L+1+B+NA), L = 1, 6 or 12.

Table Lookup d-modifiers: 1 = LL (lower than search argument), 2 = LE (equal), 3 = LLE (equal or lower), 4 = LH (higher), 5 = LLH (lower or higher, i.e. unequal), 6 = LEH (equal or higher), 7 = stop on any (Lookup to Any), blank = search to end of table (Lookup to End). The equal/high/low compare indicator is set from the last argument comparison.

Table Lookup end-of-table: a table field SHORTER than the search argument ends the operation and turns on the HIGH compare indicator; BAR then holds the address of the position immediately left of the short table field. Each table argument must be exactly as long as the search argument for the search to continue.

Move Characters and Edit (E aaaaa bbbbb, Autocoder MCE): the A field (data) is edited under control of the B field (edit control word / mask) and the result is left in the B field. The two fields are read alternately, character by character. Any sign in the units position of the data field is removed. A word mark is required in the high-order position of the B field to control the operation and the A field must have a defining word mark. When the A-field word mark is sensed, remaining commas in the B field are set to blanks. After: IAR=NSI, AAR=A-LA, BAR varies with the result of the edit. T = 4.5(L+1+A+1.5B+1.5Z+1.5D), L = 1, 6 or 11.

The edit control field is split into a BODY (used to punctuate the A field) and STATUS portions. The body begins with the rightmost blank or zero and continues left until the A-field word mark is sensed; everything else is status. An edit normally takes two instructions: a move to place the control word (and its word mark) into the output area, then the E instruction. The data field may contain fewer, but must not contain more, positions than the number of blanks and zeros in the body of the control word.

Zero suppression: the rightmost 0 in the control field marks the rightmost limit of suppression. Forward scan replaces control positions right of that 0 with A-field digits, replaces the 0 itself with the corresponding A digit and AUTOMATICALLY SETS A WORD MARK there, then continues until the high-order B-field word mark is sensed and removed. Reverse scan then replaces all zeros and punctuation left of the first significant character (up to and including the suppression-code position) with blanks; when the automatically set word mark is sensed it is erased and the operation ends.

Asterisk protection: an asterisk in the BODY left of the zero-suppression code causes the reverse scan to replace zeros, blanks and punctuation left of the first significant digit with asterisks instead of blanks (an asterisk in the body to the RIGHT of the suppression code is treated as a blank). Asterisk protection and floating dollar sign cannot be used in the same control field.

Floating dollar sign: a $ in the BODY left of the zero-suppression code needs THREE scans - forward scan replaces the $ with the corresponding A digit and continues to the B word mark; reverse scan blanks zeros and punctuation left of the first significant digit until the auto-set word mark; second forward scan erases that word mark, runs to the first blank position and writes $ there. The floating $ cannot be used right of the decimal point, and if decimal control is active at the same time an all-cents amount edits to '.25' rather than '$.25' (workaround: put the zero-suppression code left of the point, e.g. b$0.bb).

Sign control left: CR or - placed in the high-order STATUS position is left undisturbed if the A-field sign is minus and blanked if the A-field sign is plus. In the BODY portion CR and - are simply left undisturbed where written.
facts.source: A22-0526-2 Figure 28 p.32 and Figure 32 p.33

facts.claim: Decimal control: a point in the BODY left of the zero-suppression code makes the point print only when the field has significant digits. Two scans normally; if the field has NO significant digits a second forward scan runs and blanks the zeros right of the point and the point itself, stopping at the decimal column (result: an entirely blank field).

Edit control characters: blank = replaced by the corresponding A-field character; 0 = zero-suppression code, replaced by the corresponding A character, rightmost one sets the suppression limit; . = stays where written unless decimal control applies; , = stays where written unless zero suppression reaches it with no significant digit to its left; CR and - = body: undisturbed, status: blanked if A sign is plus, kept if minus; & = produces a blank in the output (may be used in multiples); * = status: undisturbed, body: asterisk protection; $ = status: undisturbed, body: floating dollar sign.

Compare/Table Lookup/Branch-if-Character-Equal share the same high/equal/low/unequal latches; once the B=A indicator is set OFF during an operation it cannot be set ON again for the rest of that operation.

Acceptable instruction lengths per op (CE handbook chart; * marks the interruptible length under the priority feature): A/S/?/!/@/% = 6, 11*; D = 6, 12*; Z = 6, 11*; E = 6, 11*; C = 6, 11*; T = 6, 12*; G = 7; ',' (SW) = 6, 11*; lozenge (CW) = 6, 11*; / (clear storage and branch) = 6, 11*; '.' (halt and branch) = 6; N = no operands.
facts.source: IBM 1410 CE Handbook 223-2588-2, 'Op Code Lengths' p.16-17

facts.claim: The 1410 has no separate Load, Move-and-Insert-Zeros, or Translate/Convert instruction. The 1401 'Load Characters to A/B word mark' function is expressed as D with the word-mark bit set (MLCWA / MLCWB); on the 1410 the op-code characters L and M are I/O instructions (Read/Write with and without word marks).
facts.source: A22-0526-2 Appendix pp.101-105 (complete alphabetic instruction list) and CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.16-17

facts.claim: The 1410 character set is 64 BCD code points (BA8421 plus a C check bit for odd parity; a word-mark bit is counted before the check bit is computed). Collating sequence runs from blank (lowest) upward; Figure 2 gives the full chart.

SimH's 1410-family CPU is not a file named i1410_cpu.c; rcornwell/sims implements the 1410's successor, the IBM 7010, in I7000/i7010_cpu.c with shared character codes in I7000/i7000_defs.h. Its op-code character constants match the 1410 PoO exactly (A=061, S=022, ?=072, !=052, @=014, %=034, G=067, ','=033, lozenge=074, '/'=021, '.'=073, N=045, D=064, Z=031, C=063, T=023, E=065, all octal BA8421).

SimH's 7010 accepts D and T in lengths 1, 2, 6, 7, 11 and 12 (op alone, op+mod, op+A, op+A+mod, op+A+B, op+A+B+mod) whereas the 1410 PoO documents L = 1, 6, 12 only. Treat 2/7/11 forms as 7010 latitude, not documented 1410 behaviour, unless verified separately.
facts.source: https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_cpu.c (case OP_MOV / OP_T length validation) vs A22-0526-2 p.25

facts.claim: Branch-test d-characters for the arithmetic/compare indicators: J(I)Z = arithmetic overflow (BAV), J(I)V = zero balance (BZ), J(I)W = divide overflow (BDV), J(I)S = compare equal (BE), J(I)U = compare high B>A (BH), J(I)T = compare low B<A (BL), J(I)/ = compare unequal (BU).
facts.source: A22-0526-2 Appendix pp.101-102 and Figure 35 p.36; CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.20

facts.claim: The 1410 Accelerator feature replaces every timing formula in the manual with a faster set, listed separately under '1410 Accelerator'. The base storage cycle is 4.5 microseconds per character.

tables.title: IBM 1410 instruction table - Part A (data movement, arithmetic, logic/compare, editing, word-mark/storage ops)

tables.title: Sign rules: add-cycle selection and result sign (Add / Subtract)
tables.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-2, Figures 11 and 12, p.16
tables.markdown:
**Sign is the zone bits of the UNITS position of the field.**

| Sign | BCD bits | Card code |
|---|---|---|
| Plus | no B, no A bit | no zone |
| Plus | B and A bits | 12 zone |
| Minus | B bit only | 11 zone |
| Plus | A bit only | 0 zone |

A machine-developed or machine-changed plus sign is ALWAYS written as B+A. A machine-developed minus is a B bit. Testing a result's sign is therefore done with `V (I) (B) K` (branch if zone equal B): no branch ⇒ the sign is BA, A, or none — all positive.

| Operation | A-field sign | B-field sign | Add cycle | Sign of result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Add | + | + | true-add | + |
| Add | + | − | complement-add | sign of greater value |
| Add | − | + | complement-add | sign of greater value |
| Add | − | − | true-add | − |
| Subtract | + | + | complement-add | sign of greater value (after the A-field sign is inverted by the subtract) |
| Subtract | + | − | true-add | − |
| Subtract | − | + | true-add | + |
| Subtract | − | − | complement-add | sign of greater value (after inversion) |

When a complement-add underflows, a **recomplement** pass is taken; the timing term `R` is 1 when a recomplement occurs, 0 otherwise (`+1.5RB` in the Add/Subtract formula).

**Zero and Subtract (two fields) sign map** (A22-0526-2 Figure 13, p.18):

| A-field sign | B-field sign at end |
|---|---|
| no B and no A bits (plus) | B bit (minus) |
| B bit (minus) | B and A bits (plus) |
| B and A bits (plus) | B bit (minus) |
| A bit (plus) | B bit (minus) |

**Multiply**: like signs in the units position of multiplicand and multiplier ⇒ plus product; unlike ⇒ minus. **Divide** (Figure 16, p.21): remainder takes the sign of the original dividend; quotient sign = + / − / − / + for divisor-dividend sign pairs +/+, +/−, −/+, −/−.

tables.title: Edit (op E) control characters and scan rules
tables.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-2, Figure 28 p.32 and pp.31-33
tables.markdown:
The control field is split into a **body** (punctuates the A field) and **status** portions. The body begins at the **rightmost blank or zero** and runs left until the A-field word mark is sensed; everything else is status.

| Control char | Function |
|---|---|
| `b` (blank) | Replaced by the character from the corresponding A-field position. |
| `0` (zero) | Zero-suppression code. Replaced by the corresponding A character. The **rightmost** `0` in the control field marks the rightmost limit of zero suppression. |
| `.` (point) | Remains where written, unless decimal control is in effect and the data field had no significant digit. |
| `,` (comma) | Undisturbed where written, unless zero suppression reaches it and no significant numeric character is found to its left. |
| `CR` | Body: undisturbed where written. Status: blanked (both positions) if the A-field sign is plus; undisturbed if minus. |
| `-` (minus) | Same as `CR`. |
| `&` (ampersand) | Produces a blank in the output field. May be used in multiples. |
| `*` (asterisk) | Status: undisturbed. Body: asterisk protection (see below); an `*` in the body to the RIGHT of the zero-suppression code is treated as a blank. |
| `$` (dollar) | Status: undisturbed. Body: floating dollar sign; a `$` in the body to the RIGHT of the zero-suppression code is treated as a blank. |

**Plain zero suppression (2 scans).** Forward: positions right of the `0` take A digits; the `0` itself takes its A digit and a word mark is set there automatically; scan runs to the B-field word mark, which is sensed and removed. Reverse: all zeros and punctuation left of the first significant character, up to and including the suppression-code position, become blanks; the auto-set word mark is sensed, erased, and the operation ends.

**Asterisk protection (2 scans).** Same as above except the reverse scan writes asterisks instead of blanks.

**Floating dollar sign (3 scans).** Forward scan replaces the `$` with the corresponding A digit and continues to the B word mark. Reverse scan blanks zeros and punctuation left of the first significant digit until the auto-set word mark. Second forward scan erases that word mark, runs to the first blank position, writes `$` there and stops. Cannot be used to the right of the decimal point; cannot be combined with asterisk protection in the same control field; with decimal control also active, `bb$.bO` edits `00025` to `.25`, not `$.25` (put the suppression code left of the point — `b$0.bb` — to avoid this).

**Sign control left (2 scans).** `CR` or `-` in the high-order status position stays if the A sign is minus and is blanked if plus.

**Decimal control (2 scans, 3 if the field has no significant digits).** A point in the body left of the suppression code. Reverse scan leaves the point and everything right of it alone once significant digits are found. If there are NO significant digits, a second forward scan blanks the zeros to the right of the point and the point itself, stopping at the decimal column — the field edits to all blanks.

When the A-field word mark is sensed, remaining commas in the B field are set to blanks. Any sign in the units position of the A field is removed by the operation.

tables.title: Indicators set/reset by Part-A operations
tables.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-2 p.16, p.21, p.28, p.36 and Appendix pp.101-102
tables.markdown:
| Indicator | Set by | Tested / reset by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arithmetic overflow | Add, Subtract (and any op where the result exceeds the B-field word-mark limit) — carry is lost | `J (I) Z` (BAV), or computer reset | Indexing overflow does NOT set it. |
| Zero balance | Add, Subtract, Multiply, Zero and Add, Zero and Subtract producing a zero balance | `J (I) V` (BZ); also turned off by the next arithmetic op (any except Divide) that does not give a zero balance; computer reset turns it off | Divide never affects it. |
| Divide overflow | Divide (quotient field two or more positions too small; division by zero always) | `J (I) W` (BDV), or computer reset | A quotient field exactly one position short silently corrupts the adjacent field with NO overflow indication. |
| Compare high (B > A) | Compare, Table Lookup, Branch if Character Equal | `J (I) U` (BH) | Also set when the A field is shorter than the B field in a Compare, and when a Table Lookup hits a short table field. |
| Compare equal (B = A) | Compare, Table Lookup, Branch if Character Equal | `J (I) S` (BE) | Once turned off during an operation it cannot be turned on again for the rest of that operation (CE Hbk 223-2588-2 p.24). |
| Compare low (B < A) | Compare, Table Lookup, Branch if Character Equal | `J (I) T` (BL) | Computer reset turns this ON. |
| Compare unequal | accompanies high or low | `J (I) /` (BU) | Computer reset turns this ON. |

All four compare latches are reset and re-set as a group by the next Compare, Table Lookup, or Branch if Character Equal.

tables.title: Timing formula symbols
tables.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-2, Figure 7, p.12
tables.markdown:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `A` | A-field length |
| `B` | B-field length |
| `C` | 1 if the branch is taken, otherwise 0 |
| `D` | number of characters in the B field from the start of zero suppression to the point where the dollar sign is inserted; 0 if no `$` is inserted |
| `E` | 2 on a single-character multiply or divide; 1 on a single-character add, subtract, zero-and-add, zero-and-subtract, table lookup, or on a 6-character multiply or divide; 0 otherwise |
| `I/O` | time used by the I/O device plus synchronizer access time |
| `L` | instruction length |
| `M` | multiplier length |
| `N` | number of fields actually compared on a table search (the table-search B-field length counts only argument fields actually compared plus intervening function values) |
| `Q` | quotient length |
| `R` | 1 if a recomplement is taken on an add or subtract, otherwise 0 |
| `Z` | number of characters in the B field from the start of zero suppression (as indicated in the control field) to the left end of the B field |

Basic core-storage cycle is 4.5 µs per character. All formulas give microseconds. The **1410 Accelerator** feature replaces every one of these formulas with a faster set, listed together in the manual under that heading.

open_questions: The 1410 PoO PDFs on bitsavers have no embedded text layer; every PoO citation here comes from the Internet Archive's OCR of edition A22-0526-2 (item bitsavers_ibm1410A22_13458542). Edition A22-0526-3 (the last edition) was not readable without OCR — worth a targeted page check for any changed timing formula or added d-modifier before freezing the emulator's tables.

Move Characters and Suppress Zeros: the PoO states the register results (AAR = A-LA, BAR = B+1) and the suppression rules but never states in words that the A- and B-addresses are the UNITS positions and that the copy pass runs right-to-left. This is inferred from the register results and confirmed only by the SimH 7010 implementation. Confirm against A22-0526-3 or the CE manual data-flow charts.

Whether a 1-character chained Add/Subtract/ZA/ZS behaves as the 'two field' or the 'one field' variant is not spelled out; both variants list L = 1 in their timing. The mechanically consistent reading is that a 1-char instruction always uses the current AAR and BAR (two-field behaviour), and the one-field behaviour arises from the 6-char form, where the A-address is loaded into both AAR and BAR. Needs confirmation from the CE data-flow manual.

The exact printed glyph for BCD code 16 (A bit only) — the 'substitute blank' used as the SCNLA d-character — could not be recovered from the OCR. The PoO Figure 2 shows it as a blank-like character with card code 8-2 and footnote (2); SimH renders it 'b'. The BIT PATTERN (A only) is certain; only the glyph is uncertain.

Exact PoO page numbers here are the manual's printed page numbers taken from the table of contents, the running footers, and the appendix's own PAGE column. Physical PDF page offsets were not established.

Interruptibility: the CE handbook marks the 11-/12-character forms of most Part-A ops with an asterisk meaning 'interruptible length'. The precise interrupt/resume semantics (priority feature) belong to a separate topic and were not researched here.

The 1410's floating-point feature (SimH defines OP_FP) and the 1401-compatibility feature (223-2597) add op codes outside this scope; whether any of them overload a Part-A op-code character was not checked.

No Load, Move-and-Insert-Zeros, or Translate/Convert instruction was found in the 1410 base set. This is a negative result from the PoO's complete alphabetic instruction listing (pp.101-105) plus the CE handbook op-code length chart; it is strong but is an absence-of-evidence argument.
